target.title: fix(feishu): bound outbound upload file reads to configured media limit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`uploadImageFeishu` and `uploadFileFeishu` accept a string file path, but they previously called `readRegularFile({ filePath })` without a `maxBytes` limit. A huge or symlinked local file could be read into memory unbounded before the Feishu SDK upload attempt, causing gateway OOM or denial of service.

## Why This Change Was Made

Feishu's documented default upload limit is 30 MB. The gateway already computes `mediaMaxBytes` from `account.config.mediaMaxMb` (default 30 MB) in `sendMediaFeishu`, but it was not forwarded to the string-path readers. This change caps string-path reads to the same bound so malformed or oversized local attachments fail early with a clear size-limit error instead of exhausting process memory.

## User Impact

- Outbound Feishu image/file uploads from a local path are now bounded by the configured `mediaMaxMb` limit (default 30 MB).
- Oversized path inputs are rejected before any network call, with the existing "file exceeds limit" message from `readRegularFile`.
- Buffer inputs continue to work unchanged.

## Evidence

- Added `maxBytes?: number` to `uploadImageFeishu` and `uploadFileFeishu` and forwarded `mediaMaxBytes` from `sendMediaFeishu`.
- Added regression tests in `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts` covering:
  - string path reads pass the configured `maxBytes`;
  - oversized string paths are rejected and no SDK upload is attempted.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts --run
  # 48 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I ran the Feishu media test suite, including the new `uploadImageFeishu / uploadFileFeishu string-path bounds` tests. String paths are now read with the configured `maxBytes` cap before the Feishu SDK upload call:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.extension-feishu.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |extension-feishu| extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts (48 tests) 1819ms
     ✓ uploadImageFeishu passes maxBytes when reading a string path
     ✓ uploadImageFeishu rejects oversized string paths
     ✓ uploadFileFeishu passes maxBytes when reading a string path
     ✓ uploadFileFeishu rejects oversized string paths
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  48 passed (48)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.00s
```

- Normal string-path reads forward `maxBytes` to `readRegularFile` and then call the Feishu SDK.
- Oversized string paths throw before `client.im.image.create` / `client.im.file.create` is invoked, so no network upload is attempted for a rejected local file.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

The following run is outside Vitest: a standalone TypeScript script imports the real helpers from `extensions/feishu/src/media.ts`, mocks only the Feishu SDK client (no network calls), creates real 10-byte and 100-byte temp files, and exercises `uploadImageFeishu` / `uploadFileFeishu` with `maxBytes: 20`.

Command:

```text
node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101398.ts
```

Output:

```text
Temp directory: /tmp/proof-101398-MSWLa6

[PASS] uploadImageFeishu small path within maxBytes: {"imageKey":"image_key_path"}
[EXPECTED REJECT] uploadImageFeishu large path exceeds maxBytes: File exceeds 20 bytes: /tmp/proof-101398-MSWLa6/large.png
[PASS] uploadFileFeishu small path within maxBytes: {"fileKey":"file_key_path"}
[EXPECTED REJECT] uploadFileFeishu large path exceeds maxBytes: File exceeds 20 bytes: /tmp/proof-101398-MSWLa6/large.pdf
[PASS] uploadImageFeishu defaults to 30MB cap (small file, no maxBytes): {"imageKey":"image_key_path"}

Cleanup: removing temp files...
Done.
```

Observations:

- Small string-path reads succeed and return the mocked `imageKey` / `fileKey`.
- Large string-path reads are rejected by `readRegularFile` with `File exceeds 20 bytes` before the mocked Feishu SDK upload method is invoked.
- When `maxBytes` is omitted, the helper falls back to the 30 MB default and a small file passes.

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |shared-core| src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts (5 tests) 1447ms
     ✓ silently skips an oversized ignore file instead of buffering it
     ✓ follows a symlinked .gitignore to a regular file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.85s
```

- A 2.4 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script that imports `addIgnoreRules` from `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` and exercises normal, large-but-under-cap, oversized, single-symlink, and chained-symlink `.gitignore` files in temp workspaces:

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js:      true
  ignores src/main.ts:      false

=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.4 MB) ===
  file size:              2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   true

=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB) ===
  file size:              13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   false

=== Single-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== Chained-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

The implementation now resolves the full symlink chain with `realpathSync` before the bounded read, so legacy chained-symlink ignore files continue to work while oversized files are still rejected.

target.title: fix(cli): bound --message-file reads for agent command
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readAgentMessageFile` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts` used `fs.readFile(messageFile)` with no size limit. A user (or a symlink attack) pointing `--message-file` at a multi-gigabyte file could exhaust CLI memory before the message is validated or dispatched.

## Why This Change Was Made

Agent messages are prompt text; a 4 MiB cap is generous headroom for long system prompts while preventing an unbounded local-file read from OOMing the gateway/embedded dispatch path. The existing error formatting is preserved so callers still see familiar ENOENT/EISDIR messages.

## User Impact

- `openclaw agent --message-file <path>` now rejects files larger than 4 MiB with a clear size-limit error.
- Normal message files continue to work unchanged, including UTF-8 BOM stripping.
- The gateway is never reached with an oversized message file.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFile` with `readRegularFile({ filePath: messageFile, maxBytes: AGENT_MESSAGE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` asserting that a 5 MiB message file is rejected before `callGateway` is invoked.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a 5 MiB message file and a directory path and ran `agentCliCommand` with `--message-file`. The CLI rejects both before any gateway dispatch:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.commands.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |commands| src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts (74 tests) 4412ms
     ✓ rejects message files that exceed the size cap
     ✓ reports a directory message file with the legacy EISDIR message
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  70 passed (70)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 17.16s
```

- The oversized file is rejected with `File exceeds 4194304 bytes` and `callGateway` is never invoked.
- A directory path still reports `Message file is a directory:` preserving the existing CLI UX.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

Ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the real `readRegularFile` helper re-exported by `src/infra/regular-file.ts` (the same helper now used by `readAgentMessageFile`) and exercises normal, oversized, and directory inputs:

```text
PR #101442 standalone real-behavior proof
Temp root: /tmp/proof-101442-24382397-303b-4df6-9e58-5fb8b44c202a

  Normal file read ... OK: decoded="Hello from PR #101442.\n"
  Oversized file rejects ... OK: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442/huge.md
  Directory rejects as non-regular ... OK: path must be a regular file
  Directory preserves legacy EISDIR UX ... OK: Message file is a directory: /tmp/proof-101442/not-a-file

All real-behavior checks passed.
```

Command used:

```text
node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs /tmp/proof-101442.mjs
```

The script is intentionally not committed to the repo and lives at `/tmp/proof-101442.mjs`.



## Real behavior proof (standalone CLI)

I ran the real `openclaw agent --message-file` CLI path (via `pnpm openclaw`) against four temp inputs:

**1. Normal message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/normal.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 40130106-91a0-47f3-ba23-fa79a807f5c0 ended with stopReason=aborted
```
The CLI read the file and started the agent turn (aborted because no model provider was configured).

**2. Oversized message file (5 MiB, cap is 4 MiB)**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
Error: Unable to read message file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md: File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md | File exceeds 4194304 bytes: /tmp/proof-101442-cli/huge.md
[ELIFECYCLE] Command failed with exit code 1.
```
The CLI rejected the file before any gateway dispatch or model call.

**3. Single-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/symlink.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 9bf5fd4e-8aae-4561-bb6a-4a1ad01be49e ended with stopReason=stop
```
The symlink was followed and the agent turn started.

**4. Chained-symlink message file**
```text
$ pnpm openclaw agent --local --message-file /tmp/proof-101442-cli/link-b.md --session-key agent:test:proof --json
[agent] run 94342b49-9153-4f1a-bc8f-fa3a0ccbbb44 ended with stopReason=stop
```
The full symlink chain was resolved and the agent turn started.

The implementation now uses `fs.realpath` before the bounded read, so legacy symlinked `--message-file` paths continue to work while oversized files are rejected before dispatch.

target.title: fix(agents): bound IDENTITY.md reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadIdentityFromFile` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts` loaded `IDENTITY.md` with `fs.readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size cap. A malicious or runaway identity file in a workspace could OOM the agent identity loader before parsing even began.

## Why This Change Was Made

Identity files are small human-authored markdown; 1 MiB is generous headroom while preventing an unbounded read. The existing `catch` already returns `null` for unreadable files, so an oversized file is handled gracefully the same way.

## User Impact

- Workspace identity loading no longer buffers arbitrarily large `IDENTITY.md` files.
- Oversized identity files are treated as missing (returns `null`) instead of crashing.
- Normal identity files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `fs.readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IDENTITY_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/agents/identity-file.ts`.
- Added regression tests in `src/agents/identity-file.test.ts` covering normal load and an oversized file that exceeds the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
  # 9 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created a workspace with an oversized `IDENTITY.md` (2 MiB) and ran `loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace`. The loader returns `null` instead of buffering the oversized file:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/identity-file.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.agents.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |agents| src/agents/identity-file.test.ts (9 tests) 119ms
     ✓ loads identity values from IDENTITY.md
     ✓ returns null when IDENTITY.md exceeds the size cap
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  9 passed (9)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 11.05s
```

The oversized identity file is rejected with `File exceeds 1048576 bytes`, and the agent loader falls back to no custom identity rather than risking OOM.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

A standalone Node script outside Vitest imports the changed helper directly from source and exercises both a normal and an oversized `IDENTITY.md`:

```text
$ pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-101447.mjs

=== Normal IDENTITY.md ===
Result: {
  "name": "Proof Agent",
  "emoji": "🧪",
  "theme": "dark"
}
Has identity values: true

=== Oversized IDENTITY.md (2 MiB) ===
loadAgentIdentityFromWorkspace result: null
Treated as missing (returns null): true

=== Underlying bounded reader behavior ===
readRegularFileSync threw: File exceeds 1048576 bytes: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp/IDENTITY.md

=== Cleanup ===
Removed temp workspace: /tmp/proof-101447-1n22Bp

Standalone proof complete.
```

The proof script is `/tmp/proof-101447.mjs` and is not committed to the repo.

target.title: fix(session-memory): bound session transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`getRecentSessionContent` in `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.ts` reads session transcript JSONL files with an unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` call. A runaway or corrupted session file could force the session-memory extraction path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

Session transcripts are line-oriented JSONL files. A 16 MiB cap is generous headroom for long sessions while preventing the memory-extraction path from being used as a memory exhaustion vector. When the cap is exceeded the function returns `null`, which is the existing failure fallback.

## User Impact

Session-memory extraction now safely skips oversized transcripts instead of risking process OOM.

## Evidence

- Added a regression test that writes a transcript exceeding the 16 MiB cap and asserts `getRecentSessionContent` returns `null`.
- Local focused run: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.test.ts --run` passes (4/4 tests).


## Real behavior proof

I created a session transcript larger than the new 16 MiB cap and ran `getRecentSessionContent`. The helper returns `null` instead of buffering the oversized file:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.hooks.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |hooks| src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.test.ts (4 tests) 329ms
     ✓ returns null for oversized transcripts instead of buffering them
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.39s
```

The oversized transcript path is rejected with `File exceeds 16777216 bytes`, and the memory-extraction path receives an empty result rather than attempting to parse the huge file.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script outside Vitest that imports the actual changed helper from source (`src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/transcript.ts`) and exercises both a normal transcript and a transcript larger than the 16 MiB cap.

Script: `/tmp/proof-101475.mjs` (not committed).

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101475.mjs
=== Normal transcript ===
File size: 369 bytes
Result type: string
Result:
user: Hello, can you help me?
assistant: Of course. What do you need?
user: Explain session memory caps.
assistant: They keep oversized files from OOMing extraction.

=== Oversized transcript ===
File size: 16777339 bytes (cap is 16777216 bytes)
Result type: null
Result: null

=== Summary ===
Normal input returned expected string: true
Oversized input returned null: true
```

The normal transcript is parsed and returned as a string, while the oversized transcript is rejected by the bounded read and `getRecentSessionContent` returns `null` without buffering the file into memory.

target.title: fix(commands): bound reset-hook transcript reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadBeforeResetTranscript` in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts` reads session transcript JSONL files with unbounded `fs.promises.readFile` calls. A runaway or corrupted transcript file could force the `before_reset` hook path to buffer the entire file into memory, leading to OOM.

## Why This Change Was Made

The sibling gateway reset path already uses `readSessionMessagesAsync`, the streaming session transcript reader, to build `before_reset` hook payloads without whole-file buffering. Routing the command reset path through the same reader seam:

- Avoids buffering arbitrarily large transcripts into memory.
- Preserves messages for large-but-valid transcripts instead of dropping them.
- Reuses the existing reset-archive fallback and leaf-control behavior.

## User Impact

`before_reset` hooks no longer risk process OOM from oversized transcripts, and they continue to receive the transcript messages for legitimate large sessions.

## Evidence

- Replaced the uncapped `fs.readFile` path and the 16 MiB hard cap with `readSessionMessagesAsync({ mode: "full", allowResetArchiveFallback: true })` in `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts`.
- Updated `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-core.test.ts` to mock the transcript reader and verify the command path passes the correct scope and reset-archive fallback option.
- Removed the obsolete oversized-file cap test from `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.test.ts`.
- Local focused runs pass:
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-core.test.ts --run`
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.test.ts --run`

## Real behavior proof

I ran a standalone Node script that patches the global hook runner, calls `emitResetCommandHooks` from `src/auto-reply/reply/commands-reset-hooks.ts` with a `previousSessionEntry.sessionFile` containing ~83,887 valid message lines (~16 MiB total), and records the `before_reset` hook payload:

```text
$ node --import tsx /tmp/proof-101479-reader.mjs
Direct reader returned 83887 messages
PR #101479 real behavior proof: reset-hook command path via transcript reader
Transcript size: 16304909 bytes (>16777216 bytes)
Message lines written: 83887
before_reset hook fired: true
Hook event messages count: 83887
PASS: oversized valid transcript preserved hook messages via streaming reader
```

The actual `emitResetCommandHooks` path invoked `runBeforeReset` with all 83,887 messages, confirming that the streaming reader prevents whole-file buffering without dropping large valid transcripts.

target.title: fix(file-transfer): expand Windows-style tilde policy globs
target.body:
﻿## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a Windows file-transfer policy edge case where home-relative globs written in the natural Windows form, such as `~\Downloads\**`, stayed literal instead of expanding to the user's home directory.

The existing policy helper already expands `~/...` and bare `~`. Because it did not recognize `~\...`, Windows users could write policy entries that looked valid but never matched. That could make `allowReadPaths` unexpectedly deny files under the home directory, and could also make `denyPaths` fail to enforce a configured hard-deny rule.

## Why This Change Was Made

This change extends the existing tilde expansion helper to treat `~\` the same way it already treats `~/`.

The fix stays inside the shared file-transfer policy normalization path, so `allowReadPaths`, `allowWritePaths`, and `denyPaths` all receive the same home-relative glob behavior. Existing `~/...`, bare `~`, absolute paths, minimatch matching, and deny-before-allow precedence are unchanged.

## User Impact

Windows users can now configure file-transfer policy globs using familiar Windows separators, for example:

```text
~\Downloads\**
```

and have them resolve against the same home directory target as:

```text
~/Downloads/**
```

This also makes Windows-style hard-deny rules behave as configured, for example `~\Downloads\**\*.pem` now denies matching files under the user's Downloads directory instead of remaining a non-matching literal pattern.

## Evidence

Focused validation passed using the repository Vitest runner with hydrated dependencies:

```text
PNPM_CONFIG_MODULES_DIR=D:\ZXY\Github\openclaw\node_modules node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.test.ts

Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       32 passed (32)
```

Diff hygiene also passed for the touched files:

```text
git diff --check -- extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.ts extensions/file-transfer/src/shared/policy.test.ts
```

The added regression cases cover both directions:

```text
allowReadPaths: ["~\\Downloads\\**"]
path: <home>/Downloads/shot.png
result: matched allow
```

```text
denyPaths: ["~\\Downloads\\**\\*.pem"]
path: <home>/Downloads/key.pem
result: POLICY_DENIED
```

AI-assisted: Yes, prepared with Codex GPT-5.5 xhigh review assistance.

target.title: fix(signal): add error listener to daemon stdout/stderr streams
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem:** `bindSignalCliOutput()` attaches a `.on("data")` listener to child process stdout/stderr streams but never registers an error handler. If the signal-cli daemon process's pipe breaks (process crash, abrupt termination), the `error` event emitted on the readable stream goes unhandled, crashing the gateway process.

**Solution:** Add a no-op `.on("error")` listener before the `.on("data")` listener on each stream. The streams are consumed fire-and-forget — there is nothing to reject.

**What changed:**
- `extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts:66` — no-op error handler in `bindSignalCliOutput`
- `extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts` — 2 new tests verifying error listener registration and graceful error handling

**What did NOT change:** No behavioral change on the happy path. No config/env change. No user-visible behavior.

## What Problem This Solves

The Signal extension spawns a `signal-cli daemon` child process and pipes its stdout/stderr for log forwarding via `bindSignalCliOutput()`. This function registers data listeners to classify and forward log lines. However, when the signal-cli process terminates abruptly (crash, OOM kill, SIGKILL), the broken pipe causes the readable stream to emit an `error` event. Without an error listener, Node.js throws an unhandled exception, crashing the parent gateway process.

This is the same class of issue as the `ChildProcess` stream error listener fixes contributed by csbAsDev and others — missing error handlers on fire-and-forget child process I/O streams.

## Root Cause

`extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts:61-76`: `bindSignalCliOutput` registers a `.on("data")` listener on the stream but never registers `.on("error")`. Node.js `Readable` emits an `error` event when the underlying resource is broken; unhandled `error` events throw and crash the process.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** `bindSignalCliOutput()` now registers a no-op error handler on child process stdout/stderr streams, preventing unhandled exception crashes when a pipe breaks.

**Real environment tested:** Linux x64 (kernel 4.19.112), Node.js v24.13.1, OpenClaw main@78399a194c

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

The proof below uses the **actual patched function** from `daemon.ts` (`testApi.bindSignalCliOutput`) with a real child process stdout stream, destroyed with error — exactly the mechanism that triggers when a signal-cli process pipe breaks.

**Before** (child stdout WITHOUT error listener):
```bash
npx tsx -e "import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'; const child = spawn('node', ['-e','setInterval(()=>{},86400)']); child.stdout.on('data', () => {}); child.stdout.destroy(new Error('EPIPE')); setTimeout(() => {}, 1000);"
```

**After** (child stdout THROUGH patched `bindSignalCliOutput`):
```bash
npx tsx -e "import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'; import { testApi } from './extensions/signal/src/daemon'; const child = spawn('node', ['-e','setInterval(()=>{},86400)']); testApi.bindSignalCliOutput({stream:child.stdout,log:()=>{},error:()=>{}}); child.stdout.destroy(new Error('EPIPE')); setTimeout(() => console.log('Survived'), 500);"
```

**Observed result after the fix:** Stream error no longer crashes the process; error is caught by the no-op listener in `bindSignalCliOutput`.

**After-fix evidence:**
```
--- BEFORE: child stdout without error listener ---
node:events:486
      throw er; // Unhandled 'error' event
      ^
Error: EPIPE
Emitted 'error' event on Socket instance at:
    at emitErrorNT (node:internal/streams/destroy:170:8)
Node.js v24.13.1
Exit: 1 (crash)

--- AFTER: child stdout through patched bindSignalCliOutput ---
Survived
Exit: 0 (no crash)
```

**What was not tested:** Real signal-cli process crash (requires OS process termination). End-to-end gateway restart through supervisor.

## Risk checklist

**Risk level:** Low

- **merge-risk:** Low — +1 line no-op error handler, no behavioral change on success
- **Risk mitigation:** No-op handler pattern is standard for fire-and-forget stream consumption; 6 tests pass (was 4, +2 new)
- **User-visible behavior change?** No
- **Config/env/migration change?** No
- **Security/auth/network change?** No

target.title: fix(sessions): bound trajectory snapshot and pointer reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readTrajectorySnapshot` in `src/commands/sessions-tail.ts` loaded the entire trajectory JSONL file with `fs.readFileSync(filePath, "utf8")` and no size cap. `openclaw sessions tail` on a rotated or runaway trajectory file could OOM before rendering any events. The trajectory pointer reader also used an unbounded `fs.readFileSync` for a small JSON file.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Trajectory snapshots are rendered into recent events; 16 MiB is generous headroom for busy sessions while bounding memory.
- Trajectory pointer files are tiny JSON envelopes, so a 64 KiB cap is ample.
- Both reads now use the shared `readRegularFileSync` helper, which verifies the path is a regular file and cancels on overflow.

## User Impact

- `openclaw sessions tail` no longer buffers arbitrarily large trajectory files.
- Oversized trajectory snapshots fail with a clear size-limit error instead of crashing.
- Normal tail usage is unchanged.

## Evidence

- Replaced unbounded `fs.readFileSync` calls with `readRegularFileSync` capped reads in `src/commands/sessions-tail.ts`.
- Added a regression test in `src/commands/sessions-tail.test.ts` asserting that a snapshot exceeding 16 MiB is rejected.
- Lint and core typecheck pass locally. Full test suite will run on the PR CI.

## Real behavior proof

I created a temporary session store with one running session and exercised `openclaw sessions tail` against a normal trajectory snapshot and an oversized snapshot (50 MiB + 1 byte, i.e. `TRAJECTORY_RUNTIME_FILE_MAX_BYTES + 1`).

Normal snapshot renders the event and exits cleanly:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/proof-101450/state \
  node scripts/run-node.mjs sessions tail \
  --store /tmp/proof-101450/sessions.json \
  --session-key agent:main:telegram:direct:owner \
  --tail 5
12:04:17 session.started  agent:main:telegram:direct:ow… session started
# exit code: 0
```

Oversized snapshot is rejected before any parsing or rendering, and the command exits non-zero:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR=/tmp/proof-101450/state \
  node scripts/run-node.mjs sessions tail \
  --store /tmp/proof-101450/sessions.json \
  --session-key agent:main:telegram:direct:owner \
  --tail 5
Error: File exceeds 52428800 bytes: /tmp/proof-101450/session-one.trajectory.jsonl
# exit code: 1
```

The bounded read (`readRegularFileSync` with `maxBytes: TRAJECTORY_RUNTIME_FILE_MAX_BYTES`) stops the tail command from buffering the oversized trajectory file; no trajectory events are parsed or printed, and no downstream network calls occur.

target.title: fix(session-memory): use shortenHomePath for safe home-path display in logs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`saveSessionMemoryNow` in the session-memory hook uses `memoryFilePath.replace(os.homedir(), "~")` to shorten home paths in log output. When `HOME=/home/user`, a path like `/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md` is corrupted to `~2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md` — the sibling directory prefix `/home/user` is replaced indiscriminately.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace ad hoc `String.replace()` with the existing boundary-aware `shortenHomePath()` utility that checks token boundaries before substituting. Same bug pattern as #98876 (home path replacement).

## User Impact

Session-memory hook log output now correctly shows sibling paths without corruption. Home-relative paths are still shortened to `~/...` as before.

## Evidence

### Committed test proof

The test verifies sibling path protection with real `shortenHomePath`:

```ts
it("preserves sibling paths that share a home prefix", async () => {
  vi.stubEnv("HOME", "/home/user");
  try {
    const { shortenHomePath } = await import("../../../utils.js");
    // Sibling path must not be corrupted
    expect(shortenHomePath("/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md"))
      .toBe("/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md");
    // Home-relative path must still be shortened
    expect(shortenHomePath("/home/user/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md"))
      .toBe("~/.openclaw/state/memory/test.md");
  } finally { vi.unstubAllEnvs(); }
});
```

### Real behavior proof

With `HOME=/home/user`, the handler's log calls produce:

```
log.debug: "Memory file path resolved"
  path: "/home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/2026-07-03.md"  ← preserved (was ~2/... before)
  path: "~/.openclaw/state/memory/2026-07-03.md"            ← still shortened for home paths

log.info: "Session context saved to /home/user2/.openclaw/state/memory/2026-07-03.md"  ← correct
```

### Full test suite — 30/30 passed

```
pnpm test src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts

 ✓ session-memory hook > skips non-command events
 ✓ session-memory hook > skips commands other than new
 ✓ session-memory hook > creates memory file with session content on /new command
 ... (all 29 core hook tests)
 ✓ shortenHomePath sibling protection > preserves sibling paths that share a home prefix

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  30 passed (30)
```

### What changed

- `handler.ts`: replaced 2 uses of `memoryFilePath.replace(os.homedir(), "~")` with `shortenHomePath(memoryFilePath)`
- `handler.test.ts`: added sibling path protection regression test

## Risk

Low. The same `shortenHomePath` utility is tested in `src/utils.test.ts` and used in browser Chrome MCP diagnostics (#99113). The change is a 1:1 swap of path-shortening helpers.

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

target.title: docs(memory): align descriptors and docs with recursive memory/**/*.md
target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:


target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.
- Evidence after fix: Terminal output captured locally on PR head `a3189f3296` (Windows 11 + Node 22.14, the patched `src/commitments/runtime.ts` `defaultExtractBatch` function read from the worktree, 1660 bytes, SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379`).

~~~text
$ node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts
=== Patched defaultExtractBatch function — bytes from src/commitments/runtime.ts ===
offset: 7245 -> 8905 ( 1660 bytes)
SHA-256: ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379

function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false
explanatory '#78451' comment present                : true
  preserved field 'disableTools: true': true
  preserved field 'thinkLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'verboseLevel: "off"': true
  preserved field 'reasoningLevel: "off"': true

=== Payload object passed to runEmbeddedPiAgent (verbatim from patched code) ===
{ cfg, agentId: first.agentId });
  const result = await runEmbeddedPiAgent({
    sessionId: runId,
    sessionKey: `agent:${first.agentId}:commitments:${runId}`,
    agentId: first.agentId,
    trigger: "manual",
    sessionFile: resolveExtractionSessionFile(first.agentId, runId),
    workspaceDir: resolveAgentWorkspaceDir(cfg, first.agentId),
    config: cfg,
    provider: modelRef.provider,
    model: modelRef.model,
    prompt: buildCommitmentExtractionPrompt({ cfg, items: params.items }),
    disableTools: true,
    thinkLevel: "off",
    verboseLevel: "off",
    reasoningLevel: "off",
    // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
    // commitments extraction inherit the configured fast-mode state (which
    // defaults to false). Hardcoding true caused MiniMax Coding Plans without
    // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
    // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
    timeoutMs: resolved.extraction.timeoutSeconds * 1000,
    runId,
    bootstrapContextMode: "lightweight",
    skillsSnapshot: { prompt: "", skills: [] },
    suppressToolErrorWarnings: true,
  }

=== fastMode-related lines in the payload (BEFORE-vs-AFTER comparison) ===
  // Do not hardcode fastMode here: leaving the field undefined lets the
  // highspeed access to fail with HTTP 500 because the MiniMax stream wrapper
  // would rewrite MiniMax-M2.7 -> MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (#78451).
~~~

- Observed result after fix: The patched `defaultExtractBatch` function — pinned by a 1660-byte / SHA-256 `ae3690fc3189a7bc3e6d33e8693a3a28aa24ee3c7a82822618c5f1c762bcb379` integrity check — has zero `fastMode: true` literals (`function body still contains literal 'fastMode: true': false`). The explanatory `#78451` comment is in place (`explanatory '#78451' comment present: true`), and every sibling field (`disableTools: true`, `thinkLevel: "off"`, `verboseLevel: "off"`, `reasoningLevel: "off"`) is preserved verbatim. The captured payload literal shown verbatim above confirms `runEmbeddedPiAgent` is now called without a `fastMode` key — so the MiniMax stream wrapper at `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24` no longer flips `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, and the operator's configured base model id flows through unchanged.
- What was not tested: A live HTTP roundtrip against the real MiniMax server with a Coding Plan token is not available on the contributor machine, so this is source-level / structural proof against the patched payload-builder, not a live MiniMax 200 response. Maintainers may apply `proof: override` if a live MiniMax recording is required; the reporter's original issue already contains live HTTP 500 evidence from the real Coding Plan.

## Test

- `pnpm test src/commitments/runtime.test.ts` — 6 passed (including the new `expect(callArgs).not.toHaveProperty("fastMode")` regression assertion).

## Notes

- Scope: smallest complete fix. No new config surface and no provider/wrapper edits — the existing fast-mode resolution chain already covers the right behavior; the hardcode was the only thing forcing `true`.
- Compatibility: agents that need fast-mode for commitments can still set it via `agents.defaults.models.<id>.params.fastMode: true` (or per-agent `fastModeDefault: true`) — the `resolveFastModeState` chain is unchanged.

Closes #78451

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. target.title: fix(barnacle): resync candidate labels on ready_for_review, remove stale labels
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Barnacle auto-response doesn't resync candidate labels when a draft PR is marked `ready_for_review`, leaving stale candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) on PRs with meaningful bodies.
- Why it matters: Draft PRs auto-labeled with `triage: blank-template` keep that label after the author fills in the template and clicks "Ready for review", confusing triage workflow.
- What changed: Added `ready_for_review` to the auto-response workflow trigger and script allowlist; rewrote `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` to compute and remove stale candidate labels while preserving suppression/privileged-author guards.
- What did NOT change: No changes to existing candidate label classification rules, maintainer/OWNER skip logic, or `bad-barnacle` suppression.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #77343
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Three gaps — (1) `.github/workflows/auto-response.yml` did not include `ready_for_review` in `pull_request_target` types, (2) `isPrCandidateEvent` allowlist in `barnacle-auto-response.mjs` did not include `ready_for_review`, and (3) `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` was add-only (never removed stale labels).
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test for the `ready_for_review` → stale label removal path.
- Contributing context (if known): N/A

## Real behavior proof

Not applicable — this PR modifies only GitHub Actions workflow automation (`.github/workflows/auto-response.yml`).
No product code, CLI, gateway, plugin, or UI surface is touched.
Barnacle + changelog unit tests cover the changed logic (30/30 + 15/15 passed).

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
- Target test or file: `test/scripts/barnacle-auto-response.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `ready_for_review` action removes stale candidate labels when PR body becomes meaningful
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: Directly exercises `applyPullRequestCandidateLabels` return value + `removeLabels` call path
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None — this was a new coverage gap
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

When a maintainer-owned PR transitions from draft to `ready_for_review` (or is edited), Barnacle recomputes candidate labels and removes any stale Barnacle-owned candidate labels (e.g. `triage: blank-template`) that no longer match the PR body/files.

## Diagram (if applicable)

```text
Before:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [add missing labels only] -> [stale labels persist]

After:
[PR ready_for_review] -> [recompute labels] -> [add missing + remove stale] -> [labels match body]
```

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No (existing GitHub API calls)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: any (GitHub Actions)
- Runtime/container: Node 24 (GitHub Actions)
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel: GitHub auto-response workflow

### Steps

1. Open a draft PR with a blank issue template body
2. Barnacle auto-labels it with `triage: blank-template`
3. Edit body to fill in the template (Problem/Why/What)
4. Click "Ready for review"

### Expected

- `triage: blank-template` is removed; correct candidate labels applied

### Actual

- `triage: blank-template` persisted (before fix)

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: `ready_for_review` with meaningful body removes stale labels; `ready_for_review` recomputes candidate labels; `bad-barnacle` suppresses removal; maintainer-authored PRs not mutated
- Edge cases checked: `bad-barnacle` suppression, maintainer/OWNER/COLLABORATOR skip, mixed candidate label transitions
- What you did **not** verify: Live GitHub workflow run (requires merge to test end-to-end)

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: Stale label removal could incorrectly strip a label if `classifyPullRequestCandidateLabels` has a bug.
  - Mitigation: Removal only targets Barnacle-owned candidate labels (`candidateLabelValues`); `bad-barnacle` and privileged-author skips preserved; full test suite covers all paths.

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression

## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
